name: desire for social status
quote: One day I'm gonna be somebody.
description: Wanting to be validated or better perceived by a particular social group.

variations.name: desire for validation
variations.description: Wanting to have your social value confirmed.

variations.name: desire to recover lost status
variations.description: You may perceive that you're recovering previously lost status. This may come with relief or vindication.

variations.name: desire to win
variations.description: You perceive a competition with another person or group, and want to win.

variations.name: desire for wealth
variations.description: Access to a valued asset is a sign of social status, whether that wealth is money, collectibles, fame, attractiveness, or something else.

variations.name: desire for existential status
variations.description: A desire to align with perceived expectations from the deepest elements of life, gaining grace from God, karma, or the Universe.
examples: Modern religious people may strive for goodness, faith, and charity.
Ancient religions may have encouraged aggression and bravery.

commentaries.quote: People sacrifice so many necessities of life to impress one another that they appear to be responding to a higher, spiritual need.
commentaries.attribution: Steven Pinker in 'How the Mind Works'

commentaries.quote: The deepest craving of human nature is the need to be appreciated.
Deep down people recognize that we require social support for our individual survival in the long term. So having status with a group that help keep us safe is unconciously critical.
Gaining social status with one group probably involves losing status with another. People will unfairly criticize others for the purpose of scoring points with someone.

conditions: Perception that you have not achieved optimal credit from a particular group.

1.description: Your brain predicts that a higher social status will provide chemical reward or relief from stress.
